text:
anya: quick sync after the RFC review. I'm proposing we stop sending full billing tag JSON across the edge and instead emit a fixed-size "attrib token" that points to a mapping in the ingest tier. thoughts?

kevin: sounds promising for envelope size, but we need clear limits on what goes in the token (no freeform fields).

anya: exactly. token will encode a 128-bit id, a version byte, and a small enum set (model_family, variant_tag, quant_enum). that's it. token base64 length ~22 chars.

maria: how do we handle on-the-wire validation? do we sign tokens or rely on mapping store checks?

anya: sign with an HMAC keyed at edge, include 4-byte checksum to catch corruption. mapping entries are created at issuance time so ingest can reject unknown tokens.

jong: collision math? we need numbers to present to SRE. Also what happens to telemetry/dashboards that expect tags immediately?

anya: collision prob with 128-bit id is negligible; we'll still check on write. dashboards: ingest keeps an LRU cache of token->tags. If miss, metric falls into unattributed_{tenant} stream and we backfill later. Alerts fire if unattributed rate spikes.

kevin: retention: storing mapping for 90 days by default, with enterprise opt-in for longer. be explicit about per-entry byte cost in RFC.

maria: GDPR: token must not be reversible to PII. use salted hash of tenant id and rotate salts carefully.

anya: rollout plan: dual-write period where agents emit both token + full tags for 48h. monitor mapping hit rate and error budget. flip feature flag after 24h of stable >99% hits.

obs-bot: checklist ticket created: https://internal/redwood/ops/tickets/AT-452 :white_check_mark:

kevin: good. i'll draft the RFC addendum with perf targets and microbenchmarks (C++/Go decode cost). pairing with jong for load tests.

anya: thanks all. i'll open the PR with exact token layout, signing scheme, and the rollout checklist.
